title: Midweek ops: micro-postmortem rollout talking crib
content:
Purpose: quick internal announcement and Q&A crib for a short (5–7 minute) sync to introduce a lightweight micro-postmortem workflow for small incidents. This is a personal scratchpad — keep conversational, short, and action-oriented.

Background notes to self:
- Problem: small incidents clog SRE bandwidth and full PM pipeline; low-severity repeats slip through. We need a faster loop so we learn without heavy ceremony.
- Goal: introduce a 15–30 minute micro-postmortem for incidents meeting simple criteria, plus a short template and a cadence for review.
- Why now: repeated cache-eviction flaps and a couple of noisy alerts this quarter. Leadership OK with lighter docs for <1hr impact incidents.

Quick talking points (opening, 60–90s):
- Lead-in: "Heads up — we’re trying a faster way to capture learnings for small incidents so we can fix recurring friction without creating paperwork."
- What: "A micro-postmortem is a focused 15–30 minute writeup that captures timeline, root cause, immediate mitigation, and one follow-up action."
- When to use: "For incidents that (a) had <1 hour user impact or service degradation, (b) didn’t require cross-org war room, and (c) have a single, actionable follow-up. If in doubt, opt for full PM."
- Why it helps: "Less context switching, faster fixes, and it surfaces patterns to our oncall rotation and SRE leads."

One-liner framing to read verbatim if asked: "Think of micro-PMs as short, focused memory for the team — they’re not a replacement for thorough investigations when needed, but they help us stop doing the same small mistakes over and over."

Canonical micro-postmortem template (to paste into Confluence / GH Issue):
- Title: incident-date - short description
- Severity / duration: e.g., Sev3, 23m impact
- Timeline (3–5 bullet timestamps)
- Root cause (1–2 lines)
- Mitigation / rollback performed
- Follow-up action (one owner, by-date)
- TL;DR (3–4 word takeaway)

Checklist: when to escalate to a full PM
- multiple services affected or >1 hour impact
- regulatory / data exposure risks
- unclear root cause after micro writeup
- cross-team blocked work needing deep analysis

Anticipated questions (Q) + short answers (A)
Q: "Won’t this just add more tickets?"
A: "We expect fewer, shorter docs. The template is intentionally minimal; ops leads will close trivial follow-ups in weekly triage."

Q: "How do we avoid noise?"
A: "Micro-PMs go to a dedicated space and are reviewed weekly by SRE leads to identify repeats; repeated patterns trigger full investigations."

Q: "Who owns the micro-PM?"
A: "The oncall engineer files it; SRE lead confirms follow-up owner if needed."

Q: "Is there a retention requirement?"
A: "Keep for 90 days as a default, longer if it identifies a recurring issue. We’ll set a Confluence TTL later."

Ops play (action items I need to do before announcement):
- Draft Confluence micro-PM template (Marta) — target: Thu EOD
- Create GH issue type / label for micro-PMs (Ethan) — target: Fri midday
- Short runbook entry in #ops-runbooks (me) — target: Friday standup
- Add micro-PM review to Friday SRE leads agenda (ask Tomas)

Tone notes (personal):
- Keep it light, emphasize experimentation and rollback: "we’ll try this for 6 weeks and iterate"
- Avoid blaming language — focus on process speed and learning
- Use two quick success criteria: fewer repeat incidents; average closure time <72h for follow-ups

Sample opening script (for 5 min sync):
- "Quick update: trying a micro-postmortem process for small incidents. Why: reduce context switching and speed fixes. Who: oncall files, SRE lead reviews. When: for incidents under 1 hour and not cross-org. We’ll run this as a 6-week experiment and measure repeats. Ask your oncall to use the template and tag #ops-runbooks."

Notes on metrics to report back after pilot:
- count micro-PMs/week
- percent that escalate to full PM
- median time from incident -> follow-up closure
- number of recurring incidents identified

Open questions / decisions (to resolve):
- TTL for micro-PM retention (propose 90 days)
- Do product/CS need to be cc’d on every micro-PM? (suggest: only if user-visible impact)
- Where should micro-PMs live? Confluence or GitHub issues? (lean GH for traceability)

Closing reminders to self:
- Keep announcement under 3 minutes, then open for 2–4 Qs.
- Push template link in channel immediately after event.
- Follow up with a 1–pager in Confluence summarizing pilot results at 3 and 6 weeks.

Draft Slack ping (1–2 lines) to drop after sync: "Quick pilot: micro-postmortem process for small incidents — template here <link>. Oncall: please file micro-PMs for <1hr incidents. SRE leads will triage weekly. We’ll evaluate in 6 weeks. Questions?"

Personal scratch TODOs:
- Finalize template + link
- Loop in Tomas and Ethan for tooling + agenda
- Rehearse 60s opener
- Post channel ping immediately after sync

End of scratchpad. Keep terse; will convert to a tidy announcement doc if leadership greenlights.
